title: Evergrove — partner opportunity ramble
content:
Quick note: this is a freeform brain dump on Evergrove — retail platform (mid-market chain, ~120 stores + ecommerce). Putting everything here so we can iterate before formalizing a one-pager. Expect half-formed hypotheses and trade-offs.

One-liner hypothesis
- Evergrove cares about reducing customer service cost and improving conversion on product detail pages. A small embed+chat surface + fast hosted inference could win a low-friction pilot. If they have tighter compliance needs (PCI adjacent / customer PII), Dedicated or Private will be the natural upsell.

Account snapshot (what I found quickly)
- HQ: Minneapolis. Funding: series B-ish (public headlines).
- Tech: React e-comm frontend, Node-based backend, uses Snowflake for analytics, and Segment -> Braze for email. Likely AWS-hosted; mentions EKS in job postings.
- Signals: job posting for "AI personalization engineer" in late 2024; marketing blog about "improving search relevance" in Q1 2025.
- Commercial: mid-market pricing bands; cares about margins and unit economics (retailers are trained to watch margins).

Key stakeholders to map / who to find on LinkedIn
- Head of Customer Experience (decision-backer for CS/chat).
- Director of Personalization / Search (technical champion for embeddings / rerank).
- Head of Platform / Infra (security + Private deployment questions).
- Head of Digital Merchandising (business owner; cares about conversion and A/B tests).

Initial value props to test (short, crisp)
- "Cut support time by X% with an LLM chat that surfaces order, returns, and SKU info — no manual macros." (tie to $ savings)
- "Add an affordable semantic search layer (embeddings) to boost PDP conversion by surfacing related items + questions."
- "Route to lightweight on-prem/Dedicated if you must keep PII on-prem; start on hosted to show ROI fast."

Signals that suggest good conversion risk and timeline
- They already hire ML infra / personalization folks -> faster POC (2–6 weeks).
- High volume of return/customer service queries in forums/blogs -> good ROI case for chat.
- If they have strict vendor security reviews, timeline expands (8–16+ weeks).

Possible pilot shapes (ranked, with minimal ops friction first)
1) Hosted API + small chat widget fed by Segment / product catalog -> 30-day pilot. Low lift.
2) Embeddings-powered search rerank on PDP (A/B test) -> 6–8 week experiment, needs engineering time to instrument metrics.
3) Shared Dedicated pool (monthly commit) for predictable latency if we want to run high QPS test across multiple stores -> needs procurement sign-off.
4) Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) for PII-heavy workflows -> long pole, enterprise legal + security involvement.

Outbound subject lines / email drafts (experiment variations)
- Subject A: "Idea for Evergrove: semantic search that lifts PDP conversion"
- Subject B: "Quick ROI test: reduce order-support tickets with a lightweight chat"

Email draft — version 1 (short, value first)
Hi <First>,
I noticed Evergrove mentioned improving search relevance — quick idea: run a 30-day test that adds a semantic rerank + small chat for order/returns. Typical lift we see in retail is 2–6% CVR and 20–30% fewer support contacts for answered order queries.
No infra changes required to start (hosted API). If you want we can scope a tight success metric and a one-month pilot.
— Samira (Redwood Inference)

Cold LinkedIn message (short)
- Hi <Name> — I work at Redwood Inference; we help retailers run LLM features for search and support with low latency and predictable costs. Could I share a 1-pager with a quick pilot idea for Evergrove?

Follow-up cadence (hypothesis)
- Email 1 (value + ask for 15m)
- Follow-up 3 days: short social proof + 1 concrete pilot proposal
- Follow-up 7 days: offer data ask + technical contacts to speed evaluation
- Final ping 2 weeks later: ask if they'd like to loop in procurement/SEs

Objections (prep & rebuttals)
- "We can't send PII to hosted vendors." -> Rebuttal: start with non-PII rerank + chat for product questions; provide architecture options (prefix filtering, token redaction). For sensitive workflows propose Dedicated / Private in parallel with pilot to get security buy-in.
- "We can't afford vendor fees right now." -> Rebuttal: pilot-first with narrow success metrics and time-limited evaluation; show cost model and expected ROI (ticket reduction math). Offer usage cap and monitoring.
- "Latency / customer experience concerns." -> Rebuttal: show Redwood latency profiles + can place routing to closer region. Offer a canary test on low-traffic segment.
- "We already have an internal ML team." -> Rebuttal: partner: we provide serving, autoscaling, and observability; they keep models/customization. Pitch as "plug-and-observe" rather than replacement.

Data & technical ask for a pilot (what to request from Evergrove)
- sample product catalog (CSV) + top 100 search queries
- support ticket examples (anonymized) for order/returns
- traffic per hour for candidate pages
- existing search logs / click-through to measure A/B impact

Demo checklist (small, focused)
- 1-slide ROI summary (tickets saved, conversion delta)
- Live demo: chat answering 5 example order/return queries using product catalog
- Quick embed: show semantic rerank hitting PDP in <1s for top-k
- Ops preview: cost per 1k requests / escalation path / fallback policy

Negotiation levers (what we can flex)
- Commit length: 1-month pilot -> 3/6/12-month scale-up (offer discounted commit for 6+ months).
- Support bundling: include 20h SE time for integration at pilot price.
- Observability retention: short retention during pilot, longer in paid contract.

Internal checklist / next actions
- [ ] Find Contact: Director of Personalization at Evergrove (Jason to find).
- [ ] Draft one-pager + ROI calc (Samira) -> attach to outreach sequence.
- [ ] Create a sandbox dataset: synth product catalog sample for demo (Priya)
- [ ] Seed Slack thread #prospecting-evergrove with initial message and ask for 15m intro.
- [ ] Create JIRA ticket PROSP-641 and link artifacts (Jason)

Notes / heuristics to remember when pitching retailers
- Always tie to incremental margin (don't talk only about gross revenue).
- Use operational KPIs (tickets per 1k orders) rather than abstract ML metrics.
- Bring a low-effort, measurable pilot — they like short windows and tight success criteria.

Unresolved/open questions
- Do they have a vendor security questionnaire (VSA) that triggers Private deployment? If yes, get copy early.
- Who owns search? Product or commerce engineering? Need to map org.
- Is there appetite for A/B testing on PDP (some retailers avoid changes during seasons)?

Misc notes / snippets to keep
- If pushback on cost: "Start with a 2-week experiment on a single high-value SKU cluster — show delta before wider rollout."
- Example testimonial to use: "Reduced order support load by 28% in 8 weeks — national apparel chain" (we should verify before using).

End ramble. Will formalize into one-pager once we have contact and get green light for a 15m intro.

— Samira
